messages:
maya: Heads-up — antlia21b int4 canary is hitting OOMs on long replies (slowgen). Observed on 3/5 of canary instances, memory fragmentation spikes after ~8k generated tokens.
lucas: logs?
maya: pasted sample stack: `OOMError: cuda out of memory while allocating KV cache slot 172...`
maya: Repro steps: canary requests with `max_new_tokens: 10000` and multi-turn history, batch_size=4. Prefetch enabled. Mem snapshot attached -> fragmentation pattern matches holey allocator behavior.
jihoon: ok. two levers: lower default max_new_tokens for antlia21b + per-model reservation (reserve 10%) before prefetch + shrink batching window for longgen traffic.
maya: +1. Also int4 seems to increase fragmentation vs int8 on this arch.
emma: propose quick patch — per-model config:
```
{
  "model": "antlia21b",
  "defaults": {
    "max_new_tokens": "1024",
    "batching": {"max_batch_size": 2, "max_wait_ms": 8},
    "prefetch": false,
    "memory_reserve_percent": 10
  },
  "fallback_order": ["antlia21b-int4","antlia21b-int8"]
}
```
lucas: we should also add a runtime guard: if request.max_new_tokens > 2048 && generation_time > 5s/token -> fail fast with suggestion to lower max_new_tokens. Avoids tail OOMs.
infra-bot: Deploy plan: push config canary to 5 hosts, monitor OOM rate, console alert on >2 OOMs/10m. Rollout window 30m.
maya: QA: run eval suite for quality on int8 fallback to verify no major regressions. qa-bot will run smoke now.
qa-bot: started evals on int8 fallback, ETA ~12m :hourglass: 
jihoon: if smoke passes, schedule canary patch tonight at 02:00UTC. Keep opt-out flag for customers needing huge generations.
maya: thanks all. I'll open a tiny PR with the config + runtime guard. tagging @emma for review :pray:
emma: review done, minor docs tweak. :thumbsup:
